questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country, rich on culture and nature; Ireland seemed like a perfect fit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In the upcoming weeks you will receive a weekly mail with all the information you'll need from UL. If you had any questions, they were very helpful and quick to respond.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an orientation week for all erasmus students where we were introduced to Irish culture, UL in general and many new friends from all over the world through several events and workshops throughout the week. It was a very nice start and I met most of my friends during this week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very friendly and helpful! Do not hesitate to ask for help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately I didn't receive an on campus accommodation offer, so I had to find it for myself. Extremely stressful process due to the housing crisis! I was lucky and found accommodation relatively nearby the university - about 15-20 minutes on bike in Garryowen. Several other international and Irish students were forced to live more than hour away from school. You can't really afford to be picky

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would maybe consider looking for off campus accommodation before you know whether you received an offer on campus or not. The sooner the better. I found my host through Hosting Power. It was expensive, but I lived with a very nice Irish lady and her dogs - she gave me tons of insights to Irish life, which was very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They are receiving way more exchange students, than they are able to accommodate :-(

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is easy and they will walk you through it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First week of school you are able to try all the courses you are interested in. By week three or so you have to apply for the courses you want to apply to. You have to make sure that all courses has been formally approved by the home university and registration will be on their platform "brightspace". You need to take a surplus of courses at from you own departing (For instance, I had to choose three psychology courses out of five)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a lecture where they described the process during orientation week and they were available on mail and in office if you needed any further help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It had no issues with registering courses. Some of the classes had a limited amount of spaces for exchange students, but I didn't seem to be any problem getting a spot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend as much as possible during the first weeks. It was a great help when choosing your final courses. They'll explain all the mandatory assessment to pass the course, which gave you a great indication of the workload for each course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my experience workload was higher than in KU as you have to take five courses, but at a bit easier level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It differed a lot depending on the size of the course. In big courses you'll typically have two hours of lectures (either consecutively or spread out over two days) and then one mandatory tutorial. Smaller courses you have lectures and tutorials in one, where discussion and team work was a big part of the teaching style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PM4035 - Psychology of Work (Arbejds- og organisationspsykologi) 
PM4013 - Principles of Human Resource Management (Arbejds- og organisationspsykologi) 
PS4031 - Psychology and Everyday Life (Valgfag)
PS4045 - Advanced Research Methods (Avanceret forskningsdesign og videnskabsteori) 
PS4097 - Developmental Psychopathology (Valgfag)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interest in clinical psychology I will recommend you to take Developmental Psychology - it offered a lot of interesting debates and guest lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot of money on Uber home from town when busses wasn't running anymore.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Hostels could be a bit expensive during prime time - but definitely worth the money if you want to explore beautiful Ireland.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many options! I was a part of the surf and kayak club. Fun, social and a good opportunity to meet irish students and to go on weekend trips around Ireland. Craft was very nice and cozy as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will recommend all of the listed clubs from before. Specifically kayak was fun as you get to go on the lake and not just the pool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around Ireland! It is easy to rent a car or go by bus. I had great time in Galway and Killarney, but I have so many other "must visit" places. I also went to Northern Ireland and Scotland - plane tickets are quite cheap from Ireland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone was so nice and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to pubs and mingle - that's the favorite irish thing to do. And join clubs! They'll throw social events and weekend trips, where you get to meet others. Participate in as many events as you can handle during the orientation week as you can handle - people are all seeking friends and are more approachable.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't really think of any. Maybe they way they dress for going out - shorts dresses throughout the whole year (rain was not holding them back).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly the irish people were and the beautiful hikes!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for a very difficult process in finding accommodation if you don't succeed with on campus accommodation. Apply for housing elsewhere before or as soon as you receive a rejection letter. If you need a bike, you by one at the UL market on in the beginning of the semester. It's a bit pricey, but very easy and he offers to take it back for half of the price at the end of the semester. 

Ireland is a very proud country with a lot of history - be careful when choosing religious and historical topics :-)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Bring rainwear and hiking boots.

If you want to use the pool facilities at UL you have to wear a swimming cap - so bring one from home if you already have one. Otherwise I visited Decathlon quite a few times. They have it all and to a quite decent price as well.

Also it's very cheap to go the cinema there. It was a nice thing to do with friends, when you were a bit socially exhausted, but still wanted to do something. 

If you are lucky enough to have nice weather while you are there; take a swim in Shannon River. There is a "beach" on campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All my friendships and hikes a achieved during my stay. I loved the cozy pub culture as well and all the live music.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Searching for off campus accommodation was rough. Try to communicate with other students going to Ireland as well - maybe you can help each other? That was a game changer for me at least.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
